title: HelixWorks Redwood Private pilot - week 6 network & upgrade check-in
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on on-prem kernel upgrade canary, routing fallback behavior, KV cache regressions on quantized models, and next-week dry-run cutover. Agreed to run targeted tail-latency benchmarks, deliver a hotfix kernel build, and schedule a constrained canary on one rack. Security asked for additional audit log detail; Redwood to share SOC2 addendum and KMS integration notes.
topics: fallback routing and circuit breaker thresholds
KV cache miss pattern after quantization
egress shaping for VPC egress bursts
security controls: KMS/HSM and audit logs
action_items: Samira Patel | Send hotfix kernel build (v3.1.2-hotfix) and install instructions | 2027-03-23
Ethan Morales | Run scripted tail-latency benchmark against quantized 7B model and share results | 2027-03-24
Maya Thompson | Provision one rack for constrained canary and confirm network ACLs | 2027-03-22
Sofia Diaz | Provide list of required audit fields for compliance review | 2027-03-25
Ben Li | Collect p95/p99 traces from current pilot and upload to shared telemetry sheet | 2027-03-24
next_steps: Redwood to push kernel hotfix to staging and give rollback playbook
Customer to run canary on single rack next Tuesday in maintenance window
Joint run of 30k token synthetic workload focused on prefix-KV cache stress
Share SOC2 controls mapping and KMS integration notes
Follow-up sync after benchmarks with remediation plan
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-20 15:21 UTC (58 mins)
Attendees: Samira Patel, Ethan Morales, Lina Cho, Marco Rivera - Redwood; Rajesh Kumar, Maya Thompson, Oliver Grant, Sofia Diaz, Ben Li - HelixWorks

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok uh thanks everyone for jumping on, um we'll try to keep this tight, we've got an hour. quick agenda: canary kernel upgrade status, routing fallback observations, kv cache/tail lat issues post-quant, and security/telemetry asks. any additions?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Rajesh): no that sounds right. maybe also timeline for cutover, customers team wants clarity on rollback steps.
00:26 Speaker 1 (Samira): perfect, i'll hand to ethan to give the upgrade readout and the hotfix status.
00:31 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yeah thanks samira. quick summary - in staging we observed a one-off p99 spike when serving quantized-7b during long prefix sessions. root cause looks like a kernel memory fence where the kv cache garbles pointer offsets under a certain batch alignment. it's intermittent but reproducible with our synthetic prefix workload. we've prepared a hotfix build v3.1.2-hotfix that avoids the fence by short-circuiting that path and reduces the tail substantially in our runs. caveat: we haven't run it under Helix's production traffic profile yet.
01:05 Speaker 4 (Maya): can you say that again? kv cache garbles... we saw a lot of unexpected cache misses last week that correlate with longer prefix contexts, that's what we were worried about.
01:13 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yep, exactly. it's a subtle alignment bug that shows up when batch sizes hit 64 and sequence length > 2k, the kv indices can shift in a way that leads to cache misses and then a high-latency regen path. please note some of the automatic correction logic in the runtime mis-labels the path as 'fast-path' so logs are noisy.
01:39 Speaker 5 (Ben): quick question - is this related to the quant kernels you pushed last sprint? we did switch to int4 microkernels.
01:46 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, the quantization changes altered memory layout and the microkernel's contiguous buffer assumptions, which exposed the alignment issue. it's not a regression in quant accuracy, it's operational.
01:58 Speaker 2 (Rajesh): ok so what's the plan for canary? we can't risk our whole cluster.
02:04 Speaker 1 (Samira): we propose a constrained canary: one rack, one model shard, maintenance window, with circuit breakers tightened and an immediate rollback hook. maya, can your team spin up the rack and confirm ACLs?
02:14 Speaker 4 (Maya): we can. i'll need the exact build and a checklist for ingress/egress rules, also burst egress shaping so our firewalls aren't tripped.
02:22 Speaker 1 (Samira): noted, ethan will send the build link and the install checklist.
02:27 Speaker 3 (Ethan): i'll also include a small wrapper script to collect per-request KV hit rates and tail-lat histograms, that should make it obvious if the hotfix works.
02:38 Speaker 6 (Sofia): on security - we need more audit fields in the logs. currently we don't capture token-level request ids tied to KMS operations and we need SSO automation steps for the on-prem control plane.
02:51 Speaker 7 (Lina): we have a page in the private docs about KMS integration but i'll send a trimmed addendum specific to Heli xWorks with exact field names.
02:59 Speaker 6 (Sofia): also, can we get an HSM flow doc? our auditors will ask about key rotation on the appliance.
03:06 Speaker 7 (Lina): absolutely, we'll share the HSM/KMS flow and rotation cadence doc.
03:12 Speaker 5 (Ben): one more note - during the last upgrade attempt we saw retries on inter-node RPCs, i think caused by MTU mismatch when the kernel toggled jumbo frames. is that addressed in hotfix?
03:23 Speaker 3 (Ethan): the hotfix doesn't change MTU settings, it's purely at the runtime execution path. however the install checklist will call out recommended nic settings and we'll include a note about jumbo frames and NIC offloads.
03:35 Speaker 2 (Rajesh): can you run the benchmark that reproduces the p99 spike with our traffic profile? the synthetic runs might not catch some pathologies.
03:44 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, we can. request: can helix share a small anonymized trace or tokenized prefix distribution? then we'll replay it in staging.
03:54 Speaker 5 (Ben): we can export a 10-minute prefix sample and scrub payloads. i'll upload to the shared folder.
04:01 Speaker 1 (Samira): great, so action items are clear. moving on to routing/fallback - marco, do you want to summarize what you saw?
04:09 Speaker 8 (Marco): sure. we configured the fallback to a smaller model variant when latency breaches p95 for 10 seconds. in last week's overlay we saw the fallback trigger but requests kept queueing on the primary for a short window, causing a second spike. looks like the router's drain timeout was too long and upstream capacity didn't free up. recommendation: reduce drain timeout from 30s to 8s and add a soft-circuit on burst egress.
04:37 Speaker 2 (Rajesh): if we shorten drain we risk more context loss for in-flight sessions, how's state preserved?
04:42 Speaker 8 (Marco): good point. sessions that rely on prefix kv cache will need a rewarm after fallback; but the trade is fewer long tail events. you can pair shorter drain with a per-session sticky routing for 5 requests to avoid immediate context loss.
04:55 Speaker 3 (Ethan): we'll also update the routing policy to record the fallback cause in traces so we can postmortem.
05:02 Speaker 4 (Maya): regarding egress shaping - we saw intermittent firewall backpressure. any chance the Redwood control messages to the private agent are too chatty?
05:12 Speaker 7 (Lina): we've been optimizing control plane chatter; we'll throttle heartbeats during heavy inference windows. we'll provide exact heartbeat cadence values.
05:20 Speaker 6 (Sofia): auditors asked for immutable tamper-evident logs, do you support write-once audit sinks?
05:28 Speaker 7 (Lina): yes, we can stream to your WORM-compliant bucket or to your on-prem SIEM; we'll include configuration examples.
05:36 Speaker 2 (Rajesh): ok timeline? if we get hotfix by Tuesday, can we do canary Wednesday night?
05:42 Speaker 1 (Samira): we aim to push to your staging tomorrow, full canary Wednesday in your maintenance window. rollback plan is to redeploy previous runtime and force a warm-start policy.
05:52 Speaker 5 (Ben): fine but i want the playbook step-by-step, not just notes.
05:56 Speaker 1 (Samira): understood - ethan will create the playbook and i'll send it.
06:00 Speaker 2 (Rajesh): great. any blockers on the SOC2 docs?
06:06 Speaker 7 (Lina): we'll attach the SOC2 addendum and a KMS mapping doc to the ticket.
06:10 Speaker 1 (Samira): ok let's recap quickly - samira: send pricing note? (crosstalk)
06:14 Speaker 3 (Ethan): pricing aside, action items we listed - hotfix, benchmarks, canary provisioning, audit fields.
06:21 Speaker 1 (Samira): perfect. thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the canary window and a short runbook. we'll reconvene after the benchmark results.
06:30 Speaker 2 (Rajesh): thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings, e.g., 'kv' marked as 'k-v' in logs, 'Redwood Private Orchestrator' sometimes transcribed as 'orch' or 'orchest'. The team agreed to tighter circuit breaker windows and a single-rack constrained canary as next step.
